baseline_note: Figs 5 and 6 SHARE ONE SOFFIT BASELINE at plate y=772 - the engraver drew a single continuous line across both. That, not a shared figure, is why connected-component isolation returned x[667,1246]. The two dimension lines abut at x~1004-1010, which fixes the figure boundary.
visual_check: Cycle 25 overlay (docs/blender/paley_pl1_fig6_overlay.png). The reconstruction now tracks the engraved boundary closely along the soffit, the 44.2 deg chamfer, the arris cusp, the whole bowtell (lower-left, bottom, right flank landing on the stock edge) and the upper hollow and chamfer. OPEN: a hatched diagonal band lies up-left of the reconstruction, running from about plate (995,737) up to (1185,642). Either it is fig 5's mass encroaching past its own dimension line (which stops at x=1010), or it is a fig-6 member not yet accounted for. Not guessed at - queued.
open_question_resolved: CYCLE 26. The hatched diagonal band up-left of the reconstruction is NOT fig 5 encroaching: fig 5's mass ends at plate x=999-1003 across y615-675, matching its own stock edge at x=1007. The band is FIG 6'S OWN UPPER FACE, which the reconstruction never traced - near-horizontal at plate y~722 (2.9 deg over x1004-1100), 46 px = 2.08 in above the soffit, then stepping up to y~690 by x=1170.
structural_note: A MOULDING SECTION IS A CLOSED OUTLINE, NOT AN OPEN PROFILE CHAIN. Fig 6's stone is bounded on BOTH sides - soffit below at y=772, upper face above at y~722 - and the reconstruction traces only the lower boundary. The `stock` field was the right instinct (a section is stone REMOVED from a block) but the member chain describes an open curve. Either the members must close the loop, or the format needs an explicit distinction between the MOULDED FACE and the bounding planes of the block.

upper_face.status: MEASURED but NOT yet in the member chain

cycle27.boundary_traced: 1168-point Moore trace of fig 6's hatched mass (contour.py, local-mean threshold 172).
cycle27.bead_confirmed: The bowtell is a real member, not a line drawn inside solid stone. Sampling 8 px inside vs 8 px outside its fitted circle at 12 angles: VOID outside at 60/120/150/210/270 deg (upper-left, left, bottom); abutting stone elsewhere, where it meets neighbouring members. Interior reads a consistent 145-149; true void reads 174-177.
cycle27.silhouette_is_not_the_profile: The traced mass silhouette CANNOT be used as the profile. It merges (a) separate members wherever they touch, (b) the stock box's DRAWN top edge at y=567, which is a box line and not stone, and (c) fig 5, via the soffit baseline they share. Line-tracing (cycles 24-25) gives the profile; the mass is only good for deciding which side of a line is void.
cycle27.two_faces: Fig 6 has TWO engraved faces, both measured, and the profile records only one. UPPER: a continuous line from plate (1000,723) rising right through (1117,710), (1160,702), (1185,637), (1213,597) to the stock's top-right corner (1242,591) - this is the same line cycle 26 measured as the 'upper face at y~722', and it runs into the 40.9 deg chamfer. LOWER: the chain already modelled - soffit, 44.2 deg chamfer, arris cusp, bowtell.
cycle27.format_decision: Members should NOT close the loop. The moulded face is an open chain; the block's bounding planes close it, and `stock` already holds the block. The real gap is that fig 6 carries TWO faces and the profile holds one. Which is the moulded face and which the bed is NOT yet established, and is not asserted.

cycle28_frame_correction.source: Paley's own text, leaf 8 of the letterpress (IA manualofgothicmo00pale_0), quoted verbatim in the docstring of moulding_profile.py
cycle28_frame_correction.axes_were_swapped: Paley: the wall-line is drawn 'parallel with the bottom of the page, and the soffit parallel to the side'. So in fig 6 the HORIZONTALS (y=772 and the upper line) lie in the WALL-plane, and the VERTICAL right edge at x=1241 is the SOFFIT. Cycles 22-27 called the bottom horizontal 'the soffit'. It is the wall-line.
cycle28_frame_correction.chain_order_was_backwards: Paley: 'a pencil were to be carried along the wall-line FIRST, and afterwards in and out of each cavity and round each projection.' The format documented soffit-first and justified it as 'the order a mason works and the order Paley lists'. He lists the opposite.
cycle28_frame_correction.hatching_meaning: 'shaded on the part which represents the level surface of the flat side of the stone' - the hatched region is the SAWN FACE, i.e. the cut section itself. Its boundary, minus the wall-line and soffit segments where the saw passed, is the moulded edge.
cycle28_frame_correction.two_faces_dissolved: The cycle-27 question - which of the two faces is the moulded one - was MALFORMED. Since the hatched region is the sawn section, both traced stretches are parts of ONE continuous moulded edge running around it. They were never rival candidates.
cycle28_frame_correction.scale_caveat: Paley suggests reducing a traced outline to 'a scale of an inch to a foot'. That is advice to the READER copying mouldings, NOT a statement about his plates - and the measurements refute it as one: fig 5 is 23.75 px/in and fig 6 is 22.09 px/in on the same sheet.
cycle28_frame_correction.next_confirmation: fig. 10, Plate 2 (leaf 92) labels a = chamfer-plane, n = soffit-plane, c = wall-plane.

frame.wall_line: HORIZONTAL, plate y=772 - parallel with the bottom of the page
frame.soffit: VERTICAL, plate x=1241 - parallel with the side; the bowtell's fitted right extreme lands on it
frame.traversal: WALL-LINE FIRST, then in and out of each cavity and round each projection (Paley's own order)
frame.note: Confirmed by eye on Plate 2 fig 10 (cycle 29): A labels the diagonal = chamfer-plane, B labels the vertical = soffit-plane. The engraved labels are rotated capitals; the OCR's 'a/n/c' are misreads of A/B/C.

skew_calibration.method: Use the figure's OWN known-horizontal (wall-line) and known-vertical (soffit) straight boundary runs as an internal angular reference. Longest-straight-run detection on the traced contour finds them without any guessed window.
skew_calibration.plate_I: skew +0.1 deg mean (runs at 179.5, 2.2, 0.8, 179.1, 90.0, 89.0, 90.0) - effectively unskewed, noise floor ~+/-1 deg
skew_calibration.plate_II: skew -1.5 deg mean (runs at 178.4, 179.2 horizontal; 87.8 vertical)
skew_calibration.consequence: Plate I's 44.2 and 40.9 deg chamfers stand UNCORRECTED. Plate II's readings need +1.5 deg.

chamfer_plane_quantified.real_moulding_pl1_fig6: 44.2 and 40.9 deg, unskewed, against a +/-1 deg noise floor - 40.9 is 4 deg off 45 and real
chamfer_plane_quantified.reading: Paley's 'generally (not invariably) done at an angle of forty-five degrees' is now quantified. His DIDACTIC figure is a clean 45. The mouldings he RECORDED FROM BUILDINGS depart from it by up to ~4 deg. So a generator should not hard-code 45, nor treat the deviation as drafting noise: sample around 45 with a few degrees of real scatter.
chamfer_plane_quantified.frame_confirmed_a_third_way: On BOTH plates the longest straight runs are horizontal and vertical: Plate I fig 6's two longest are 127 px at 179.5 deg (the wall-line) and 80 px at 90.0 deg (the soffit at x=1249); Plate II fig 10's are 109 px at 178.4 deg and 51 px at 87.8 deg. Paley's frame recovered from pixels alone, with no reading involved.

scale: UNSCALABLE - fig 7 carries NO dimension line. See scale_search.
scale_search: The only dark-fraction spike anywhere near fig 7 is y=771, and inspection at 5x shows it is the figure's STOCK-BOX bottom edge: dashed, but with no arrowheads and no label. Since cycle 23 established that scale on this plate is PER-FIGURE (fig 5 = 23.75 px/in, fig 6 = 22.09), fig 6's scale may not be borrowed. Fig 7 therefore yields SHAPE but not SIZE.
straight_run_signature: Longest runs: 103 px at 89.4 deg, 87 px at 1.3, 51 px at 3.4, 43 px at 91.3, 43 px at 88.7, 37 px at 0.0, 36 px at 88.4, 34 px at 5.0. ALL wall-plane or soffit-plane. Exactly ONE candidate in the chamfer band (38.7 deg) and it is most likely an arc chord.
vocabulary_contrast: This is the finding. Fig 6's principal member sits on a CHAMFER; fig 7 has NO chamfer-plane member at all. Its mouldings are developed by sinking hollows in the wall- and soffit-planes only - a direct illustration of Paley's 'by sinking hollows in any one of these surfaces, a group of mouldings would be developed'. Two adjacent figures on one sheet, two different generative strategies.
skew_note: Fig 7's near-horizontal runs spread 0.0-5.0 deg and its near-verticals 88.4-95.4 - about +/-5 deg, against fig 6's +/-1 deg on the SAME plate. So that spread is real member variation, not page skew. REFINEMENT: skew is a property of the PLATE - measure it on the figure with the TIGHTEST run distribution and apply it plate-wide. Plate I = +0.1 deg, from fig 6.
